title: Reproduce and investigate
outcome: Reproduce one limited research result and run an ablation, an experiment that removes one component.

blocks.body: Question: Can you recover a result and explain a failure?
Mathematics: Apply confidence intervals, seed variability, multiple-comparison caution, and controlled comparisons.
Dataset: Reuse the frozen soccer datasets and splits. For reproduction, use the selected paper’s public data if feasible; otherwise label the soccer experiment as an adaptation.
Reading: If pretrained weights or hardware are unavailable, reproduce an evaluation comparison using your existing models and label the adaptation.

blocks.title: Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model · 2025
blocks.note: Read the question, evaluation design, and limitations. Reproduce one feasible comparison, not the original training run.

blocks.title: Why Large Language Models Fail at Tabular Prediction · August 2026
blocks.note: Treat this preprint as a claim to examine. Compare its evaluation choices with your soccer experiments. No paid API experiment is required.

blocks.body: Challenge: Explain which conclusion your data supports and which it does not. Rerun one result from a clean command.

tasks.prompt: Freeze data and code versions. Implement the selected experiment with a baseline and an explicit compute limit.
